raw_segments.text: Antony, since Cleopatra died, I have lived in such dishonor that the gods detest my baseness.
I that with my sword quartered the world, and o'er green Neptunes back with ships made
cities, condemn myself to lack the courage of a woman, less noble mind than she which,
by her death, our Caesar tells, I am conqueror of myself.
Thou art sworn, Eros, that when the exigent should come, which now is come indeed, when
I should see behind me th, inevitable prosecution of disgrace and horror, that on my command
Dot, the time is come, thou strix not me, tease Caesar thou defeatst thee, put colour
